title: HBM4 Evidence Release 001
description: Research-candidate findings and proposed Atlas relationships for HBM3E, HBM4 and HBM4E. Nothing in this file is a published Atlas relationship; every candidate requires named human review against the cited passages before it may be moved into data/dependency-atlas.json.

findings.statement: JEDEC announced JESD270-4 (HBM4) on 2025-04-16 with a 2048-bit interface, transfer speeds up to 8 Gb/s and total bandwidth up to 2 TB/s per stack.

evidence.locator: JEDEC release text as surfaced by a search index on 2026-11-09; jedec.org returned HTTP 403 to direct retrieval, so the passage has not been read in full

findings.scope: Industry standard as announced; not a statement about shipped products
limitations: Pending direct review of the JEDEC text
JEDEC lists a later JESD270-4A revision (Dec 2025) whose changes are not reviewed

findings.statement: JEDEC states that HBM4 doubles the independent channels per stack from 16 (HBM3) to 32, each with two pseudo-channels.

evidence.locator: JEDEC release text as surfaced by a search index on 2026-11-09; jedec.org returned HTTP 403 to direct retrieval, so the passage has not been read in full

limitations: Pending direct review of the JEDEC text

evidence.locator: JEDEC release text as surfaced by a search index on 2026-11-09; jedec.org returned HTTP 403 to direct retrieval, so the passage has not been read in full

findings.scope: Industry standard as announced; permitted configurations, not products offered
limitations: Pending direct review of the JEDEC text

findings.statement: JEDEC states HBM4 remains compatible with HBM3 controllers, so one controller can support both, and adds Directed Refresh Management (DRFM) for row-hammer mitigation.

evidence.locator: JEDEC release text as surfaced by a search index on 2026-11-09; jedec.org returned HTTP 403 to direct retrieval, so the passage has not been read in full

limitations: Pending direct review of the JEDEC text
Controller compatibility does not imply drop-in substitution at the package or platform level

findings.statement: SK hynix reports that its HBM4 doubles bandwidth through 2,048 I/O terminals and operates at over 10 Gbps, which it contrasts with a JEDEC standard operating speed of 8 Gbps.

evidence.locator: "the bandwidth doubled through adoption of 2,048 I/O terminals"; "over 10Gbps"; "far exceeded the JEDEC* standard operating speed(8Gbps)"

limitations: Company-reported speed; no independent measurement
No absolute per-stack bandwidth figure is given

findings.statement: Micron reported shipping 36GB 12-high HBM4 samples in June 2025 with a 2048-bit interface, greater than 2.0 TB/s per stack, built on its 1-beta DRAM process.

evidence.locator: "Micron HBM4 features a 2048-bit interface, achieving speeds greater than 2.0 TB/s per memory stack"; "Built on its well-established 1ß (1-beta) DRAM process"

Sample stage only

findings.statement: Micron reported in March 2026 that its HBM4 achieves over 11 Gb/s pin speeds and bandwidth greater than 2.8 TB/s per stack.

evidence.locator: "With HBM4, Micron achieves over 11 Gb/s pin speeds"; "enabling a bandwidth greater than 2.8 TB/s"

limitations: Footnote: internal testing and confidential customer test-vehicle validation
Does not restate interface width or DRAM process

findings.statement: Samsung reported in March 2026 that its HBM4, built on its sixth-generation 10nm-class (1c) DRAM process, delivers 11.7 Gbps, which it describes as exceeding the industry standard of 8 Gbps, and can be enhanced to 13 Gbps.

evidence.locator: "By leveraging the most advanced sixth-generation 10-nanometer (nm)-class DRAM process (1c)"; "delivering consistent processing speeds of 11.7 gigabits-per-second (Gbps), which exceeds the industry standard of 8Gbps, and can be enhanced to 13Gbps"

limitations: Company-reported speed
Per-stack bandwidth for HBM4 is not stated in this release

findings.statement: Samsung reported shipping 12-layer, 48GB HBM4E samples in May 2026 with a stable 14 Gbps pin speed scalable to 16 Gbps and up to 3.6 TB/s per stack.

evidence.locator: "a stable pin speed of 14 gigabits-per-second (Gbps), with performance scalable up to 16Gbps"; "up to 3.6 terabytes-per-second (TB/s) per stack"

limitations: Sample stage only
HBM4E I/O count is not stated
No JEDEC HBM4E document is cited

findings.statement: Per-stack bandwidth equals interface width times per-pin rate divided by eight. At 2,048 bits, 8 Gb/s gives 2.05 TB/s, 11 Gb/s gives 2.82 TB/s, 14 Gb/s gives 3.58 TB/s and 16 Gb/s gives 4.10 TB/s. The disclosed vendor figures are arithmetically consistent with a 2,048-bit interface, including Samsung's HBM4E figures, which do not state an I/O count.

evidence.locator: JEDEC release text as surfaced by a search index on 2026-11-09; jedec.org returned HTTP 403 to direct retrieval, so the passage has not been read in full
"over 11 Gb/s pin speeds"; "greater than 2.8 TB/s"
"14 gigabits-per-second"; "up to 3.6 terabytes-per-second (TB/s) per stack"
HBM4E: "16Gbps per pin and 4.0 terabytes-per-second (TB/s) bandwidth"

findings.scope: Arithmetic on disclosed figures; decimal terabytes
limitations: Consistency is not proof that HBM4E keeps a 2,048-bit interface
Peak interface bandwidth is not sustained application bandwidth
assumptions: All 2,048 data bits transfer at the stated per-pin rate

evidence.locator: "shipped the samples of 12-layer HBM4"; "adopted the Advanced MR-MUF process to achieve the capacity of 36GB"; "more than 2TB (terabytes) of data per second"

findings.scope: SK hynix HBM4 samples as described 2025-03-19
limitations: Sample stage only
Customers not named

evidence.locator: "by shipping samples of HBM4 48GB 16H to customers"; footnote: "33% increase in capacity per HBM placement"

limitations: Samples, not volume production

findings.statement: Samsung states its HBM4E lineup is planned to expand from the 12-layer 48GB part to 32GB 8-layer and 64GB 16-layer configurations.

evidence.locator: "with plans to expand the lineup to include 32GB (8-layer) and 64GB (16-layer) configurations"

limitations: Forward-looking plan, not shipped products

findings.statement: Dividing disclosed stack capacity by layer count gives 3 GB (24 Gb) per DRAM die for 36GB 12-high and 48GB 16-high HBM4, and 4 GB (32 Gb) per die for Samsung's 48GB 12-layer HBM4E and its planned 64GB 16-layer part. Both densities match the 24 Gb and 32 Gb options in JEDEC's HBM4 announcement.

evidence.locator: "12-layer"; "36GB"
"HBM4 48GB 16H"
"48-gigabyte (GB) capacity"; "64GB (16-layer)"
JEDEC release text as surfaced by a search index on 2026-11-09; jedec.org returned HTTP 403 to direct retrieval, so the passage has not been read in full

limitations: Vendors do not state per-die density in the reviewed releases
assumptions: Every layer is a DRAM core die of equal density
The base die contributes no user-addressable capacity
GB is 2^30-style binary gigabytes as used for DRAM capacity

findings.statement: SK hynix states that HBM is made by stacking core DRAM dies on a base die featuring TSVs, that it used proprietary technology for base dies up to HBM3E, and that it planned to adopt TSMC's advanced logic process for the HBM4 base die.

evidence.locator: "HBM is made by stacking a core DRAM die on top of a base die that features TSV"; "SK hynix has used a proprietary technology to make base dies up to HBM3E"; "plans to adopt TSMC’s advanced logic process for HBM4’s base die"

limitations: MOU-stage plan; later reviewed SK hynix releases do not restate the base-die source

findings.statement: TSMC listed "N12 and N3 logic base die for HBM4" among its offerings at its April 2025 North America Technology Symposium.

evidence.locator: "N12 and N3 logic base die for HBM4"

limitations: Does not name customers or which HBM products use which node

findings.statement: Samsung describes its HBM4E as built on its 1c DRAM process with a Samsung Foundry 4nm logic base die, and as using the same combination of core and base die as its earlier HBM4.

evidence.locator: "Samsung Foundry's 4nm logic base die"; "using the same combination of core and base die"

limitations: Reading 'same combination' as referring to Samsung's HBM4 is an interpretation of the release wording; the HBM4 release itself is pending review

findings.statement: HBM4 couples the memory layer to advanced-logic fabrication. Two of the three HBM4 suppliers reviewed here disclose a logic-process base die (SK hynix via a TSMC plan; Samsung via its own 4nm foundry for HBM4E). For those suppliers, HBM4 supply depends on logic-foundry capacity as well as DRAM fabrication, a dependency SK hynix says did not exist in that form for its base dies up to HBM3E.

evidence.locator: "plans to adopt TSMC’s advanced logic process for HBM4’s base die"
"N12 and N3 logic base die for HBM4"
"Samsung Foundry's 4nm logic base die"

findings.scope: Structural dependency inference for disclosed suppliers only
limitations: Micron's reviewed disclosures do not state its base-die process or manufacturer
No capacity or allocation inference is made
Intra-company foundry supply (Samsung) and external foundry supply (TSMC) carry different dependency profiles
assumptions: SK hynix's 2024 plan was carried into production; this is not confirmed in its later reviewed releases

findings.statement: TSMC states it continues to advance CoWoS to meet AI's need for more logic and HBM, and plans to bring 9.5-reticle CoWoS to volume production in 2027, enabling 12 or more HBM stacks in a package.

evidence.locator: "continues to advance its Chip on Wafer on Substrate (CoWoS®) technology"; "9.5 reticle size CoWoS to volume production in 2027"; "enabling integration of 12 HBM stacks or more in a package"

limitations: Forward-looking; 2027 timing is a plan
Does not name which accelerators use which CoWoS variant

findings.statement: SK hynix's 2024 MOU announcement states an aim to optimise the integration of SK hynix HBM with TSMC CoWoS technology.

evidence.locator: "optimize the integration of SK hynix’s HBM and TSMC’s CoWoS®2 technology"

evidence.locator: "a new method that will enable next-generation HBM to achieve 16 or more layers while reducing heat resistance by more than 20 percent, compared to thermal compression bonding (TCB)"

limitations: Not stated as used in HBM4 or HBM4E
Company-reported thermal figure

findings.statement: SK hynix states its Advanced MR-MUF (mass reflow molded underfill) process helps prevent chip warpage and improves heat dissipation, and that it used the process in HBM4.

evidence.locator: MR-MUF "helps prevent chip warpage, while maximizing product stability by improving heat dissipation"
"adopted the Advanced MR-MUF* process in HBM4"

limitations: Company-reported process benefits

findings.statement: Suppliers report different HBM4-generation efficiency gains against different baselines: SK hynix more than 40% better power efficiency; Micron more than 20% versus its HBM3E (a 2025 simulation basis and a 2026 internal-calculator basis at 9.2 Gbps); Samsung 16% better energy efficiency and more than 14% better thermal resistance for HBM4E versus its previous generation.

evidence.locator: "power efficiency improved by more than 40%"
"over 20% better power efficiency compared to Micron's previous-generation HBM3E"
footnote: "HBM4 12H vs. HBM3E 12H at 9.2 Gbps"
"improved energy efficiency by 16% and thermal resistance characteristics by more than 14%"

limitations: Baselines, workloads and methods differ; the figures are not comparable across suppliers and must not be used to compare them

evidence.locator: "a new Integrated Voltage Regulator (IVR) for AI with 5X vertical power density delivery"

limitations: Not specific to HBM; relevant to package-level power delivery

"Following the industry's first mass production and commercial shipment of its industry-leading HBM4"; "industry's first 12-layer HBM4E samples"

findings.statement: NVIDIA states Rubin integrates up to 288 GB of HBM4 using 12-Hi stacks with up to 22 TB/s of peak bandwidth, and that HBM4 doubles interface width relative to HBM3E.

evidence.locator: "Rubin integrates up to 288 GB of HBM4 memory, driven by dedicated HBM controllers and 12-Hi stacks"; "up to 22 TB/s of peak bandwidth"; "HBM4 doubles interface width relative to HBM3e"

limitations: NVIDIA's undated Vera Rubin NVL72 product page lists 19.2 TB/s per Rubin GPU; the conflict is unresolved

findings.statement: NVIDIA stated on 2026-01-05 that Rubin is in full production and that Rubin-based products will be available from partners in the second half of 2026.

evidence.locator: "NVIDIA Rubin is in full production, and Rubin-based products will be available from partners the second half of 2026."

limitations: The release does not mention HBM

findings.statement: If Rubin's 288 GB is built from 36GB 12-high HBM4 stacks, it uses eight stacks. NVIDIA's 22 TB/s peak then implies about 2.75 TB/s per stack (about 10.7 Gb/s per pin at 2,048 bits); the 19.2 TB/s product-page figure implies about 2.4 TB/s per stack (about 9.4 Gb/s per pin). Both exceed JEDEC's announced 8 Gb/s baseline, which shows the platform relies on above-baseline HBM4 speed grades.

evidence.locator: "up to 288 GB of HBM4"; "12-Hi stacks"; "up to 22 TB/s"
"HBM4 36GB 12H"
"12-layer"; "36GB"
JEDEC release text as surfaced by a search index on 2026-11-09; jedec.org returned HTTP 403 to direct retrieval, so the passage has not been read in full

limitations: NVIDIA does not state the stack count
Which of the two bandwidth figures is current is unresolved
assumptions: Each 12-high HBM4 stack is 36GB, as SK hynix and Micron disclose for 12-high HBM4
All stacks run at the same rate

findings.statement: Micron and Samsung each state that their HBM4 is designed for NVIDIA Vera Rubin, so the platform is designed to accept HBM4 from more than one supplier. Whether supply can in practice shift between suppliers, at what qualification status and in what volume, is not established by any reviewed source.

evidence.locator: "designed for NVIDIA Vera Rubin"
"designed for the" NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform

limitations: SK hynix's reviewed releases name no platform
No qualification, share or allocation evidence was reviewed
Package-level and speed-grade differences may limit substitution
assumptions: 'Designed for' indicates an intended interoperability target, not a completed qualification

unresolved.question: Has JEDEC published an HBM4E standard, and what parameters does it define?
unresolved.why_unresolved: No reviewed source cites a JEDEC HBM4E document; Samsung's HBM4E release cites none.
unresolved.next_evidence_needed: JEDEC publication record or committee statement.

unresolved.question: What process and manufacturer does Micron use for its HBM4 logic base die?

unresolved.next_evidence_needed: Micron technical disclosure or filing naming the base-die process.

unresolved.question: Does SK hynix's production HBM4 use a TSMC-made logic base die, and on which node?

unresolved.question: What is each supplier's HBM4 production capacity, yield and customer allocation?

unresolved.question: Which suppliers' HBM4 is qualified for which accelerator platforms, and at what speed grade?
unresolved.why_unresolved: 'Designed for' statements are not qualification disclosures; platform vendors do not name memory suppliers in reviewed sources.
unresolved.next_evidence_needed: Platform-vendor or supplier disclosure of completed qualification.

unresolved.question: Is Rubin's per-GPU HBM4 bandwidth 22 TB/s or 19.2 TB/s?
unresolved.why_unresolved: NVIDIA's 2026-07-21 technical blog states up to 22 TB/s peak; its undated Vera Rubin NVL72 product page lists 19.2 TB/s per GPU and 1,400 TB/s per rack.
unresolved.next_evidence_needed: A dated NVIDIA datasheet stating per-GPU memory bandwidth and the configuration it applies to.

unresolved.question: What does Samsung's 2026-02-12 HBM4 release state, including its per-stack bandwidth figure?
unresolved.why_unresolved: The page timed out and its mirror redirected to a generic landing page during retrieval.
unresolved.next_evidence_needed: Human reviewer reads the release; promote the registry record from pending_review.

unresolved.question: What are the thermal limits of 16-high HBM4 stacks, and does reaching them require hybrid bonding?
unresolved.why_unresolved: Samsung presents hybrid copper bonding as a future method; Micron is sampling 16-high HBM4 without disclosing its stacking method; no reviewed source establishes a requirement.
unresolved.next_evidence_needed: Peer-reviewed or supplier technical paper on 16-high HBM4 thermal behaviour and bonding.

unresolved.question: Which interposer or bridge technology, substrate and assembly providers do HBM4 accelerator packages depend on?
unresolved.why_unresolved: Reviewed sources describe CoWoS generally and do not identify per-product interposer type, substrate suppliers or assembly sites.
unresolved.next_evidence_needed: Foundry, OSAT and substrate-supplier disclosures tied to HBM4 products.

unresolved.question: How are HBM4 stacks tested before integration (known-good-stack), and who performs that testing?
unresolved.why_unresolved: No reviewed primary source addresses HBM4 test flows.

unresolved.question: What is the status and scope of JEDEC's reduced-pin-count SPHBM4 effort?
unresolved.why_unresolved: The JEDEC page could not be retrieved; only a search-index summary was seen, which is not used as evidence.

candidate_nodes.label: HBM4
candidate_nodes.description: High Bandwidth Memory generation standardised by JEDEC as JESD270-4: stacked DRAM core dies on a base die with a 2,048-bit interface.

candidate_nodes.label: HBM logic base die
candidate_nodes.description: The bottom die of an HBM stack carrying the interface and control logic, made on a logic process for HBM4 by suppliers that disclose it.

candidate_nodes.label: Advanced logic foundry process
candidate_nodes.description: Logic wafer fabrication at nodes such as 12nm-class, 4nm-class or 3nm-class, as offered by logic foundries.

candidate_nodes.label: CoWoS
candidate_nodes.description: TSMC's Chip on Wafer on Substrate advanced-packaging family, used to place logic dies and HBM stacks in one package.

candidate_nodes.label: NVIDIA Rubin GPU
candidate_nodes.description: NVIDIA accelerator generation disclosed with up to 288 GB of HBM4.

candidate_relationships.statement: HBM stacks core DRAM dies on a TSV-bearing base die; for HBM4, SK hynix planned a logic-process base die and Samsung states a 4nm logic base die for HBM4E using the same core/base-die combination as its HBM4.
limitations: Micron's base-die process is not disclosed in reviewed sources
SK hynix statement is an MOU-stage plan

candidate_relationships.statement: TSMC lists N12 and N3 logic base dies for HBM4, and SK hynix planned to use TSMC's advanced logic process for its HBM4 base die.
candidate_relationships.geographic_scope: TSMC offering and SK hynix plan; not industry-wide
limitations: Does not establish which shipping products use which node
No capacity or allocation inference

candidate_relationships.statement: TSMC describes CoWoS as advancing to meet AI demand for logic and HBM, planning 12 or more HBM stacks per package with 9.5-reticle CoWoS in 2027; SK hynix aimed to optimise its HBM integration with CoWoS.
candidate_relationships.geographic_scope: TSMC packaging offering; not the only HBM integration route
candidate_relationships.temporal_scope: Disclosures dated 2024-04-19 and 2025-04-23; 2027 plan is forward-looking
limitations: Other packaging providers and routes are not assessed
The 2027 volume-production plan is not a verified outcome

candidate_relationships.statement: NVIDIA states Rubin integrates up to 288 GB of HBM4 on 12-Hi stacks; Micron and Samsung each state their HBM4 is designed for NVIDIA Vera Rubin.
limitations: Per-GPU bandwidth conflict (22 vs 19.2 TB/s) is unresolved
Supplier qualification and share are not established
